title: Machine and Archive
premise: Orsen Underhill, a disgraced navigator hauling black-market cargo through contested orbits, receives a distress signal in a language extinct since the Meridian Purge—a tongue only the dead archives aboard his own ship can translate. The signal comes from a colony ship both fleets believe was destroyed, and its survivors hold proof that the war's founding atrocity was staged. To deliver that truth, Orsen must convince two hostile fleets that a forged ceasefire he fabricates is real, while falling for Sefa, the archive-keeper who woke from the backups he has spent ten years avoiding. In the end, Orsen broadcasts the evidence and surrenders himself to buy the ceasefire time; the lie holds, the fleets stand down, and Sefa carries his name into a new archive—not as a criminal, but as the man who made peace out of fraud.
about_author: Dominic Whitlock is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio officer who spent eleven years on deep-space supply runs before turning to fiction. He writes about people who keep systems running in places no one wants to look.

chapters.title: The Quiet Hold
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Establishes his routine hauling contraband through the Kestrel Corridor and his ritual of never entering the hold where the ship's archived minds sleep. When a junior dockhand asks what's down there, Orsen lies fluently. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: A Language With No Speakers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A distress signal arrives in Old Meridian, extinct for two centuries. Orsen recognizes it because his grandmother sang him lullabies in it before the Purge trials. He should log it and move on; instead he plots an intercept course. Emotional beat: the past reaching through static.

chapters.title: What the Backups Dream
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. One of the archived minds wakes: Sefa, an archivist who died in the Purge and was restored illegally by a previous owner. She finds Orsen's ship a museum of stolen history—and finds Orsen himself terrified of her. Emotional beat: awakening as accusation.

chapters.title: The Colony That Never Burned
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Following the signal, they find the Meridian Dawn adrift but alive—two hundred survivors the histories say were massacred. Their records prove the atrocity that started the war was staged by fleet command. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Corridor
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Both fleets converge on the corridor after a patrol ship detects the Dawn's reactor leak. Orsen realizes any honest broadcast means the fleets destroy the evidence and everyone aboard. Emotional beat: the moment invisibility stops being safety.

chapters.title: Terms of Fraud
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa proposes the unforgivable: forge an authenticated ceasefire order using archived command codes she legally shouldn't possess. Orsen resists—then agrees when the Dawn's reactor begins an unfixable countdown. Emotional beat: love and complicity becoming indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Countdown in Contested Space
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The forged ceasefire freezes both fleets mid-approach while the crew races to evacuate the Dawn. A fleet intelligence officer grows suspicious of the order's provenance. Emotional beat: hope under interrogation.

chapters.title: The Lie Under Pressure
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The intelligence officer corners Orsen with proof the ceasefire is forged. Instead of denying it, Orsen shows her the Dawn's records—the real crime beneath the fake peace. She must choose between her oath and the truth. Emotional beat: duty cracking open.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. The reactor breaches as the evidence goes out on every open channel. Both fleets hold fire, stunned. Orsen stays aboard the Dawn to keep the transmission running and is caught in the blast shadow—alive, barely, surrendering to the fleet that arrives first. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: Archive of a Living Man
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, months later. The war is suspended, tribunals underway, and Orsen awaits sentencing. Sefa testifies, then opens a new archive—one that records the living, not the dead—and enters his name first. He visits her between hearings; belonging, finally, without permission. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, love inside it.
